result.title: UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute
result.summary: Looped language models can strengthen reasoning through repeated computation with shared weights, increasing execution depth without adding independent parameters. However, each additional pass increases training floating-point operations (FLOPs), making these gains more expensive to obtain. To address this cost, we propose UpLoop, a pretraining schedule that uses upcycling to train looped Transformers while exactly matching a standard dense baseline in final parameter count, total training tokens, and training FLOPs. Specifically, UpLoop begins with a shallow Transformer, progressively grows its depth by copying learned layers, and uses the computation saved early to support repeated execution of a shared middle block later in training. Experiments across model scales show improvements in language modeling and downstream performance, with the average score across 22 downstream tasks increasing from 22.99 to 27.52 at 1.3B parameters. These gains also extend to mathematical reasoning after supervised fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 UpLoop 预训练方案：先用浅层 Transformer，再通过复制已学层逐步增加深度，并把早期节省的算力用于后期重复执行共享中间块，在参数量、训练 token 数和训练 FLOPs 与稠密基线对齐的条件下训练 looped Transformer。
